title: Mijbil the Otter
book: NCERT First Flight: Textbook in English for Class X
subject: english_literature
author: Gavin Maxwell
syllabus_note: CBSE 2025-26 English Language and Literature (184): First Flight prose, Chapter 6. Assessed through extracts (5 marks), short answers in 40-50 words (3 marks) and long answers in 100-120 words (6 marks).

blocks.title: A pet that plays with taps
blocks.body:
Most people keep a dog or a cat. **Gavin Maxwell** decided to keep an **otter**, brought it from the marshes of Iraq, and flew it all the way to London. On the way, the otter escaped inside the aeroplane!

This true story shows how a wild animal and a man came to trust each other, and how clever and funny an otter can be.

blocks.title: The writer
blocks.body:
**Gavin Maxwell** was a Scottish naturalist and writer who lived at **Camusfeàrna** on the west coast of Scotland. In 1956 he travelled to southern **Iraq** and brought back an otter, Mijbil, which belonged to a species unknown to science. It was named **Maxwell's otter** after him.

His book Ring of Bright Water, from which this story is taken, made otters famous around the world.
blocks.future: Wildlife biologists, zoologists and vets study animal behaviour the way Maxwell watched Mij.

blocks.question: Mij was aloof at first but later followed Maxwell everywhere. What changed?
options: Mij slowly learnt to trust Maxwell, who was patient and caring
Mij was punished until he obeyed
blocks.explanation: Trust between an animal and a person grows with patience and kindness.

blocks.title: From the marshes of Iraq
blocks.body:
**The idea:** early in 1956 Maxwell travelled to southern Iraq. By then it had occurred to him that he would like to keep an otter instead of a dog, and that **Camusfeàrna**, his home in Scotland ringed by water, would be a suitable place for the experiment. A friend suggested that he get one from the **Tigris marshes**, where otters were as common as mosquitoes.

**Mij arrives:** Maxwell went to **Basra**, to the Consulate-General, to collect and answer his mail. There, two Arabs brought him a sack: inside was the otter he named **Mijbil** (Mij). It resembled 'a very small, medieval dragon'. Mij belonged to a race unknown to science; zoologists named it **Maxwell's otter**.

**Learning to trust:** for the first 24 hours Mij was neither hostile nor friendly, simply **aloof and indifferent**, choosing to sleep on the floor as far from Maxwell's bed as possible. On the second night he came onto the bed and slept in the crook of Maxwell's knees. Soon he followed him everywhere.

**Water and play:** Mij went wild with joy in the **bathtub**, plunging and rolling and splashing 'like a child'. Within a few days he learnt to **turn on the tap** by himself, though it took him a little longer to turn it fully on. Indoors he played for hours with a rubber ball, and invented a game of rolling it down the sloping lid of a suitcase and catching it at the bottom. Maxwell concludes that otters are like human beings: they need **company and play**.

blocks.title: What Mij's behaviour tells us
blocks.body:
| What Mij does | What it shows |
|---|---|
| stays aloof at first, then comes to sleep in Maxwell's bed | he slowly learns to trust |
| plays wildly in the bathtub, splashing and rolling | otters are water creatures who love to play |
| learns to **turn on the tap** by himself | curiosity and intelligence |
| invents a game with a rubber ball on a sloping suitcase lid | he can entertain himself and solve problems |
| tears the lining of his travel box | he panics in a closed, strange place |
| Londoners mistake him for a seal, a squirrel, a walrus and more | otters were unfamiliar to people in England |

blocks.question: How did Mij behave during his first 24 hours with Maxwell?
options: aloof and indifferent, sleeping far from Maxwell's bed
blocks.explanation: On the second night he came to Maxwell's bed.
option_feedback: He was neither hostile nor friendly.

blocks.question: Why was the otter named 'Maxwell's otter'?
options: it belonged to a species unknown to science, named after Maxwell
Maxwell bought it in a shop
blocks.explanation: Zoologists named the new race after him.
option_feedback: It was named after its discoverer.

blocks.title: Basra to London
blocks.body:
**No animals allowed:** the airline flying to England would not carry animals, so Maxwell had to book a flight to **Paris** and on to **London**, and he had to keep Mij in a **box** about eighteen inches square, placed at his feet.

**Panic in the box:** an hour before the flight, Maxwell put Mij in the box and went for a meal. When he returned, there was blood: Mij had torn at the **metal lining** of the box until his mouth and paws were bleeding. Maxwell had to rush to the airport with the otter barely calmed.

**Chaos on the plane:** on board, Maxwell opened the box to calm Mij, who escaped and ran down the aisle. There was chaos among the passengers; a woman stood on her seat screaming, 'A rat! A rat!' The **air hostess** stayed calm and kind and helped him; Mij was caught at last and returned to Maxwell's knees.

**Mij in London:** Maxwell took Mij for walks on a lead in London. People could not guess what animal he was: they suggested a baby **seal**, a **squirrel**, a **walrus**, a **hippo**, a **beaver**, a **bear cub**, a **leopard**, and even a brontosaurus. Otters were unfamiliar to Londoners.

blocks.question: Why did Maxwell have to fly to Paris first?
options: the airline flying to England would not carry animals
blocks.explanation: So he flew via Paris to London.
option_feedback: The reason was the rule on animals.

blocks.question: What did a woman passenger shout when Mij escaped?
blocks.explanation: She stood on her seat in fear.
option_feedback: She thought it was a rat.
She thought it was a rat.
She did not know what it was.

blocks.title: Words and expressions to know
blocks.body:
| Word or phrase | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **aloof** | distant, not friendly |
| **indifferent** | not interested |
| **marshes** | low, wet land |
| **crook of the knees** | the bend behind the knees |
| **pandemonium / chaos** | wild confusion |
| **sodden** | completely wet |
| **aisle** | the passage between seats |
| **ethnologist / zoologist** | scientists who study peoples / animals |

**Style:** the story is told in the **first person** with humour; Maxwell compares Mij to a child to show his playful nature.

blocks.title: Memory tricks
blocks.body:
- **Mij's route: Tigris marshes → Basra → Paris → London → (home: Camusfeàrna, Scotland).**
- **Trust timeline: day 1 aloof → night 2 in bed → follows everywhere.**
- **Clever Mij: tap, ball, suitcase lid.**
- **London guesses: seal, squirrel, walrus, hippo, beaver, bear cub, leopard.**

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.body:
1. Saying Mij was friendly from the start: he was **aloof** for the first 24 hours.
2. Saying the airline allowed pets: it did **not**, so Maxwell flew via Paris.
3. Calling Mij an ordinary otter: he was of a **species new to science**, Maxwell's otter.
4. Writing that Maxwell was a zoo-keeper: he was a **writer and naturalist**.

blocks.title: Try this in class
blocks.body: Ask students to retell the plane journey as a news report: 'Otter causes chaos on Paris flight'. They must use five facts in the right order.

blocks.title: Think and explain
blocks.body: Should wild animals be kept as pets? Give one reason for and one against, using Mij's story.

blocks.title: Where this leads
blocks.body:
- **Geography (Forest and Wildlife Resources):** protecting wild animals in their habitats.
- **A Tiger in the Zoo (poem):** another view of a wild animal kept by people.
- **Science (Our Environment):** wetlands like the Tigris marshes support many species.

blocks.title: Mastery challenge
blocks.body:
'Mij was an intelligent and playful animal.' Prove this with examples from the story in about 120 words.

**Model answer:** Mij showed intelligence and playfulness in many ways. Though aloof at first, he quickly understood that Maxwell meant him no harm and by the second night slept in the crook of his knees. In the bathroom he went wild with joy, splashing like a child, and within a few days he learnt to turn on the tap by himself. Indoors he could play alone for hours: he shuffled a rubber ball round the room and invented a game of rolling it down the sloping lid of a suitcase and catching it at the bottom. Even his escape on the plane showed how quick and curious he was. Maxwell rightly concludes that otters, like humans, need company and play.

blocks.title: Chapter summary
blocks.body:
- In 1956 Gavin Maxwell went to southern Iraq and decided to keep an otter at his Scottish home, Camusfeàrna.
- At Basra he received Mijbil, of a species new to science, later named Maxwell's otter.
- Mij was aloof at first but soon became attached, loved water, learnt to turn on the tap and invented games.
- Airlines would not carry animals to England, so they flew via Paris; Mij tore his box and escaped on the plane, causing chaos.
- In London, people could not guess what animal Mij was.

blocks.title: Exam tips
blocks.body:
- For 'intelligence' questions, give two actions (tap, ball game) and explain what each shows.
- Narrate the journey in order: box, blood, airport, escape, chaos, air hostess, London.
- Use words like aloof, indifferent and pandemonium; they score in short answers.

blocks.back: At Basra, in southern Iraq; Mij came from the Tigris marshes.

blocks.front: How did Mij behave in the first 24 hours?
blocks.back: Aloof and indifferent; he slept on the floor far from Maxwell's bed.

blocks.front: What clever thing did Mij learn in the bathroom?
blocks.back: To turn on the tap by himself.

blocks.front: Why did Maxwell fly via Paris?
blocks.back: The airline flying to England did not allow animals.
